standard_prerequisites.name: The fibre-product simplicial object
standard_prerequisites.statement: The simplicial object U with U_n the (n+1)-fold fibre product of Y over X, built naively from f : Y to X when C has fibre products (the author's example-fibre-products-simplicial-object, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the object of the statement (source lines 4877-4880).

standard_prerequisites.name: Sections and the maps s f
standard_prerequisites.statement: A section s of f with f s = id, hence an endomorphism s f of Y whose iterates appear in each degree.
standard_prerequisites.use: It produces the self map of the statement and the g^1 used in the homotopy (source lines 4876, 4887).

standard_prerequisites.name: The relations characterising a homotopy of simplicial morphisms
standard_prerequisites.statement: A family h_{n,i} defines a homotopy if and only if it satisfies the five relations with the face and degeneracy maps (the author's lemma-relations-homotopy and remark-homotopy-better, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the criterion the written-down family is claimed to satisfy (source lines 4901-4903).

standard_prerequisites.name: The functor of points
standard_prerequisites.statement: Describing a morphism of iterated fibre products by its effect on generalised points.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the language in which the homotopy is first described (source lines 4888-4897).

core_obligations: Set up the two endomorphisms: put g^0 = id_Y and g^1 = s composed with f (source line 4887).

Describe the homotopy: exhibit, for each n and each alpha : [n] to [1], the map on the n-th fibre product given by applying g^{alpha(i)} in the i-th slot, using the functor of points (source lines 4888-4897).
Reformulate as a family: rewrite those maps as the explicit h_{n,i} with h_{n,0} = id, h_{n,n+1} = (s f)^{n+1} and the intermediate terms (source lines 4898-4901).

Record the relation check: the author refers to the relations-homotopy lemma for the verification and to the remark for the fact that no extra hypothesis on the category is needed (source lines 4901-4905).

proof_roadmap.step: Introduce g^0, g^1 and describe the maps on fibre products via the functor of points.
Reformulate the description as the explicit family h_{n,i} with the stated boundary values.
Refer to the relations-homotopy lemma for the verification and to the remark for the irrelevant extra hypotheses.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-fibre-products-simplicial-object-w-section at source lines 4873-4884: if f : Y to X has a section s and U is the simplicial object built from f by iterated fibre products, then the degreewise self map (s f)^{n+1} is homotopic to the identity, so U is homotopy equivalent to the constant simplicial object X. The proof at source lines 4886-4906 writes the homotopy down: it sets g^0 = id and g^1 = s f, describes the maps through the functor-of-points as sending a tuple together with alpha in Mor([n],[1]) to the tuple with g^{alpha(i)} applied in each slot, and rewrites this as the explicit family h_{n,i} = id^{i+1} times (s f)^{n+1-i}. The author then says that these satisfy the relations of the relations-homotopy lemma and leaves that verification to the reader, pointing to the remark that no further assumption on the category is needed. The substance of the card is therefore the construction and the reformulation; the final relation check is delegated by the author, which the card records rather than hides.
